The following translations are rough and are based on standard Sumerian language and symbols. Please note that the translation can slightly differ depending on the context that isn't provided and the fact that the Sumerian language still doesn't have a definitive translation for many of its symbols.

1. From sunrise to sunset, things will be established.
2. From the dawn, heaven and earth might be established.
3. Might the name be called from time to time.
4. They who are of the highest power might make a true binding.
5. The binding vow of the goddess Inana might be made firm.
6. The binding vow of Inana might bind heaven and earth together.
7. The binding vow of the goddess Inana ... might sweep together and bring into existence.
8. By the divine authority, may those from the holy cities decide on ...
9. May the gods collectively discern and make wise decisions. 
10. May the deity of the river stir up the earth and flood it back and forth. 
11. May the deity call forth abundant fish in the streams and make the lands fruitful. 
12. The day casts a great light, the god collectively.
13. Enki, Lord of the deep underground waters, may he not make a famine, may the god's name not perish.
14. May our place be blessed with abundant flowing waters and fatness.
15. May the god of plentifulness flood it with fatness, enough for all.
16. The man who brings it, his place should not be cursed.
17. The goddess Namma will give birth, the holy mother, and should be favored by the gods.
18. May the children not be placed in wrongdoing by the god.
19. X may not arouse wrath and may not arouse destruction.
20. X may not provoke …
21. May the evil be washed clean, the hand purified. May X be made exceeding strong.
